veranderings.rede: 'Verbrand' is the usual transitive verb for using up fuel and matches 'aanhou verbrand' and 'wat ons verbrand' later in the lesson.
The lesson and the hidro-elektries definition say 'stromende water' and 'water wat stroom', so one word for the same thing is clearer for the learner.

veranderings.voor: Die wind hou op en begin later weer waai.
veranderings.na: Die wind gaan lê en begin later weer waai.
veranderings.rede: 'Die wind gaan lê' is the natural Afrikaans idiom for wind dying down; the meaning is unchanged.
AWS writes compounds as one word; this compound is not long or unclear enough to need a hyphen.

veranderings.blok: Water wat van hoog af stroom
veranderings.voor: deur groot pype af na turbines
veranderings.rede: 'af ... laer af' repeats the particle in one short sentence; 'stroom ... na turbines wat laer af staan' already says the water goes down.

veranderings.voor: Die sonpaneel is die een wat heeltemal anders werk.
veranderings.na: Die sonpaneel werk heeltemal anders as die ander twee.
veranderings.rede: 'is die een wat' copies English 'is the one that'; the direct verb with 'as die ander twee' keeps the contrast with wind and water more naturally.

veranderings.voor: Niks draai en niks brand nie.
veranderings.na: Niks draai nie, en niks brand nie.
veranderings.rede: Two clauses with their own subject and verb each need their own closing 'nie', and AWS puts a comma before 'en' between them.

veranderings.voor: Dit maak net elektrisiteit solank die lig daarop val.
veranderings.na: Dit maak elektrisiteit net solank die lig daarop val.
veranderings.rede: 'net elektrisiteit' can read as 'only electricity'; placing 'net' before 'solank' makes it limit the time, which is the intended meaning.

veranderings.voor: 'n Sonpaneel maak snags niks en minder wanneer dit bewolk is.
veranderings.na: 'n Sonpaneel maak snags geen elektrisiteit nie, en minder wanneer dit bewolk is.
veranderings.rede: 'maak snags niks en minder' is a compressed, ambiguous construction without the negative 'nie'; naming what it makes and closing the negation reads clearly.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: solank ons dit nie vinniger gebruik as wat die natuur dit aanvul nie
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: In the block 'Wat die natuur weer aanvul' this protected clause follows 'Hulle raak nie op nie', so the singular 'dit' twice refers back to the plural 'hulle' (son, wind, water); a person may want 'hulle' in this lesson's study text, though the wording is fine inside the glossary definition where the subject is singular.
